summary.intent: Run a full code quality review (reuse, quality, efficiency) on all phase 40 branch changes, fix any issues found, then commit and open a PR.
summary.outcome: Four issues were fixed (replaced custom clamp with std clamp, removed redundant step comments, flattened an unnecessary scope block, deleted dead DEFAULT_* constants), all tests passed, changes committed, and a PR was opened.

repo: Default vault settings values live in `cipherbox_core::default_vault_settings()`, not in fuse/constants.rs — the DEFAULT_MAX_VERSIONS_PER_FILE and DEFAULT_VERSION_COOLDOWN_MS constants in fuse were dead.
KeyState fields consistently use RwLock, so VaultSettings follows the same pattern by convention.
DeleteBehavior is intentionally stringly-typed to handle raw JSON input validation at the system boundary.
VaultSettings carries a version field for schema evolution, not as redundant state.
vault settings must be loaded before FUSE mount, making load_vault_settings() blocking in auth a deliberate ordering constraint rather than a concurrency oversight.

code.finding: Had a custom clamp() helper that duplicated u32::clamp() available since Rust 1.50 — deleted in favor of std.
load_vault_settings() had 5 numbered step comments that restated the code; only the ECIES caveat comment was non-obvious and worth keeping.
Had an unnecessary bare scope block around vault settings loading; flattened it and simplified pk_slice indirection to direct .as_slice().
DEFAULT_MAX_VERSIONS_PER_FILE and DEFAULT_VERSION_COOLDOWN_MS were unused anywhere in the codebase.

workflow: The /simplify skill runs three parallel review agents (reuse, quality, efficiency) and then aggregates findings before making any edits — effective pattern for avoiding redundant or conflicting edits.
Verifying compiler output and running targeted unit tests after edits before committing caught any regressions early.
Skipping false positives with explicit rationale (rather than silently ignoring) keeps the review accountable.

friction: The first /simplify invocation was interrupted by the user mid-execution before the review agents completed, requiring a full restart with additional scope ('all phase 40 work on the branch').
Multiple redundant reads of the same tool result file occurred during diff retrieval, suggesting the diff was large or required repeated access to parse.
open_items: apply_versioning() has 10 parameters — flagged as parameter sprawl but deferred; a struct wrapper was deemed premature since the function was just extracted from inline code.
load_vault_settings() runs synchronously before FUSE mount in the auth path — a concurrency opportunity was identified but skipped as marginal given the required ordering.
